display.purpose: Page and section headlines, hero copy. Outfit.

body.purpose: All paragraph copy, form labels, navigation, general UI text. Inter.

label.purpose: Role badges, section eyebrows, small referential tags. JetBrains Mono, uppercase, tracked out — the 0.75rem type-scale floor.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Default resting shadow under glass/elevated panels — a quiet second layer under translucency, never the primary depth cue.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Stronger lift for more prominently raised elements, e.g. an open dialog.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons/interactive controls nudge down one pixel on active/press for tactile feedback.

motion.name: step-pulse
motion.purpose: Pulsing ring on the current/active stage of a compliance stepper, using the Trail Amber color.

components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 36px; padding: 0 10px; background: var(--color-signal, #2f7040); color: var(--color-void, #f1f3f1); border: none; border-radius: 8px; font-family: var(--font-sans, Inter, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, transform 0.1s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-signal, #2f7040) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-signal, #2f7040); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(47 112 64 / 0.3); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Role Badge
components.description: Pill badge marking a person's role (admin/staff/client) or an application's status.
components.css: .ds-badge-role { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid var(--color-signal, #2f7040); color: var(--color-signal, #2f7040); font-family: var(--font-mono, "JetBrains Mono", monospace); font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.35; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Directory Card
components.description: Glass-surfaced row card used in the People Directory — avatar, name, and role badge, expandable on click.
components.css: .ds-card-directory { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; width: 100%; padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: 18px; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.6); border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.7); backdrop-filter: blur(24px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(24px); transition: box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-card-directory:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(47 112 64 / 0.4) inset; } .ds-card-directory:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-signal, #2f7040); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-card-avatar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; flex-shrink: 0; width: 36px; height: 36px; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgb(47 112 64 / 0.15); color: var(--color-signal, #2f7040); font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; font-family: var(--font-sans, Inter, sans-serif); } .ds-card-body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-card-name { font-family: var(--font-sans, Inter, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-bone, #1e2a1f); }

components.name: Filter Input
components.description: Text input, e.g. the Access tab's name/role filter.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Filter by name or role" />
components.css: .ds-input { height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--color-ash, #6b7264); background: var(--color-pine, #ffffff); color: var(--color-bone, #1e2a1f); font-family: var(--font-sans, Inter, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-ash, #6b7264); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-signal, #2f7040); outline-offset: 2px; border-color: var(--color-signal, #2f7040); }

components.name: Nav Link
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 9999px; font-family: var(--font-sans, Inter, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-bone, #1e2a1f); text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background: rgb(47 112 64 / 0.08); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-signal, #2f7040); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-nav-link--active { background: rgb(47 112 64 / 0.12); color: var(--color-signal, #2f7040); font-weight: 500; }

narrative.overview:
AGV Portal is an official record shot through with living green: the institutional trust of a compliance ledger, carried by a warm forest palette instead of enterprise gray. It is warm and approachable but still precise — human enough that staff and clients don't feel like they're fighting a government form, exact enough that nothing about role, access, or application status is ever ambiguous. The system explicitly avoids two failure modes: it should never read as a cold, gray enterprise dashboard, and it should never reach for bounce, gradients, or decorative flourish to manufacture warmth it hasn't earned structurally.

Depth is glass-first: frosted, translucent panels (.glass) floating over a soft green gradient wash are the system's primary depth cue, not drop shadows — shadows exist only as a quiet second layer underneath. Interaction feedback is tactile and confident: buttons press down a physical pixel on click, focus rings glow in the accent green, and directory cards pick up a signal-colored ring on hover — restrained, but never inert.

One fixed light identity — there is no dark mode, and no user-facing theme toggle exists. A single saturated accent (Forest Signal) carries almost all interactive emphasis; every other color is either neutral or role-coded (Trail Amber = in progress, Canopy Contour = resolved), never decorative.
keyCharacteristics: Warm forest/cream palette standing in for an otherwise institutional compliance product
Glass/frosted panels as the primary depth cue; shadows are a quiet second layer
One accent color only — everything else is neutral or semantically role-coded
Tactile press/focus feedback on every interactive control
A single fixed light theme; no dark mode exists anywhere in the app

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Forest Signal is the only saturated color used for interactive emphasis anywhere in the system. A second bright accent is a regression, not a design choice.

rules.name: The No Second Theme Rule
rules.body: This is one fixed light identity, not "light mode" among several — there is no dark mode block and no user-facing theme toggle. Any dark:-prefixed utility a fetched component ships with is inert by construction; it must stay that way.

rules.name: The Label Floor Rule
rules.body: 0.75rem (Tailwind's text-xs) is the smallest type size anywhere in the system. It is the type scale's own minimum, not an arbitrary cutoff — nothing renders below it.

rules.name: The Glass-Over-Texture Rule
rules.body: .glass is only ever used over the gradient wash or imagery, never over flat page background — blur against a flat color has no visual payoff and is a wasted effect.

dos: Do use Forest Signal as the only saturated interactive accent — new components should reach for it before any other color.
Do treat glass/translucency as the default way to elevate a floating panel; reach for shadow-panel/shadow-pop as a secondary reinforcement, not the primary signal.
Do give every interactive control the same press (translate-y-px) and focus-visible (2px Forest Signal outline + ring glow) treatment already standard on buttons and inputs.
Do keep role/status color-coding semantic: Forest Signal = interactive, Canopy Contour = resolved, Trail Amber = in-progress/destructive. One meaning per color.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent color or a dedicated "red" for destructive actions — this system deliberately reuses Trail Amber at different opacities instead.
Don't add a dark mode or any user-facing theme toggle — this is one fixed light identity by explicit prior decision (Phase 19 removed the previous toggle).
Don't apply .glass over flat page background — it only belongs over the gradient wash or imagery.

Don't reach for bounce/elastic easing or gradient-heavy decoration to manufacture warmth — the palette and glass panels already carry the warmth; motion should stay purposeful and restrained (respecting prefers-reduced-motion everywhere, as the codebase already does).
